skill.name: cocoindex
skill.description: Build and operate CocoIndex data pipelines for incremental AI indexing, custom transformations, vector search, knowledge graphs, and live updates.
skill.summary: Design CocoIndex flows, custom functions, queries, and operational workflows for incremental AI data processing.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most detections are documentation artifacts: CocoIndex .eval methods are not code evaluation, and Markdown backticks are not shell execution. However, the skill explicitly solicits API key values and includes examples that can expose credentials through configurable endpoints, terminal output, or process arguments. Forced reset and drop guidance also needs mandatory safeguards.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to provide API key values in conversation.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to set secrets locally through environment variables or a secret manager. Verify only variable presence, and never request or display secret values.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting commands can print database credentials or place them in process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use non-printing presence checks and protected psql service or .pgpass configuration. Do not read .env contents into terminal output.

remediation.issue: The external API example stores a plain API key and sends it to a configurable endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Use a secret manager or transient authentication entry. Require HTTPS, validate or allowlist destinations, redact configuration output, and set request timeouts.

remediation.issue: The guide supplies fixed local database credentials as a default.
remediation.suggestion: Require user-configured credentials and label development examples clearly. Do not reuse fixed defaults in shared, containerized, or production environments.

remediation.issue: Force, reset, drop, and drop-all operations can remove persistent resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, verify the target environment, scope commands to a named flow, and recommend backups before destructive operations.

content.value_statement: Building incremental AI data pipelines requires coordinated sources, transformations, targets, and operations. This skill provides CocoIndex patterns for flows, custom functions, queries, and live updates.
actual_capabilities: Design CocoIndex flows that connect supported sources, transformations, collectors, and targets.
Generate patterns for text chunking, embeddings, LLM extraction, vector indexes, and knowledge graphs.
Create typed standalone functions and configurable function executors with caching guidance.
Explain CocoIndex CLI and Python API operations for setup, evaluation, updates, queries, and live processing.
Troubleshoot flow discovery, database connections, schema changes, live updates, and concurrency limits.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, but it does not verify compatibility with the installed CocoIndex version.
External databases, model providers, credentials, packages, and service accounts must be configured separately.
Update, reset, and drop operations can modify or remove persistent resources.
Configured LLM and API providers may receive source data during embedding, extraction, or enrichment.

use_cases.title: Index Internal Documents
use_cases.description: Create an incremental document pipeline with chunking, embeddings, metadata, and a vector database target.

use_cases.title: Build Knowledge Graphs
use_cases.description: Extract typed entities and relationships from documents, then export nodes and edges to a graph database.

use_cases.title: Operate Live Indexes
use_cases.description: Evaluate, deploy, monitor, and troubleshoot flows that continuously synchronize changing sources with search targets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CocoIndex flow that reads [file types] from [directory], splits text, and exports records to [target]. Explain dependencies and required configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Build Vector Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CocoIndex pipeline for [content] using [embedding provider] and [vector database]. Include metadata, chunk settings, primary keys, and an evaluation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Custom Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typed CocoIndex custom function for [transformation]. Choose standalone or spec-executor form, explain caching, and define error handling without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Live Multi-Target System
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a live CocoIndex flow from [sources] to [targets]. Include change capture, concurrency limits, reusable query transforms, observability, rollback, and production safeguards.

output_examples.input: Index product manuals from a local directory for semantic search in Qdrant.
output: Plan: Local document source, recursive text splitting, embedding generation, and Qdrant export.
Operations: Configure credentials locally, evaluate sample output, set up the named flow, then run an incremental update.

output_examples.input: Extract people and relationships from reports into Neo4j.
output: Schema: Typed person and relationship records with stable identifiers.
Flow: LLM extraction, normalized collectors, separate node and relationship exports, and validation before update.

output_examples.input: Keep a code search index synchronized while limiting memory use.
output_examples.output: The proposed flow uses file change capture, language detection, chunked embeddings, bounded in-flight rows and bytes, and monitored live updates.

best_practices: Test transformations with evaluation before updating persistent targets.
Store credentials locally in environment variables or a secret manager, and never place secret values in prompts.
Confirm target scope and create backups before reset, drop, or schema-changing operations.
anti_patterns: Do not request API key values in conversation or print environment file contents.
Do not run reset or drop commands without explicit confirmation and environment verification.
Do not send source data or bearer tokens to unvalidated external endpoints.

faq.question: What can this skill build?
faq.answer: It can design CocoIndex flows for incremental indexing, embeddings, extraction, vector search, knowledge graphs, and custom transformations.

faq.question: Does it install or run CocoIndex automatically?
faq.answer: It provides project and operational guidance. Package installation and command execution depend on the agent permissions and user approval.

faq.question: Which sources and targets are covered?
faq.answer: Examples include local files, cloud storage, Postgres, Qdrant, LanceDB, Neo4j, and Kuzu. Availability depends on the installed CocoIndex version.

faq.question: Are API keys required?
faq.answer: Only provider-backed embeddings, extraction, or enrichment need keys. Configure them locally and never send their values through chat.

faq.question: Can flows update data continuously?
faq.answer: Yes. Live mode requires refresh intervals or source-specific change capture, plus suitable resource and concurrency limits.

faq.question: How should destructive commands be handled?
faq.answer: Evaluate first, verify the environment and named flow, back up persistent data, and obtain explicit confirmation before reset or drop operations.
